# A stated cost on a split the transaction already prices.
#
# The purchase says what the USD cost: 135.00 CAD for 100.00 USD, 1.35. The
# `cost_basis_cost:` line beside it says 9.99, and one of the two has to lose.
# Taken as authoritative, the stated cost is what `fx-balances` reports and
# what every later sale must be valued against, so a book's own figures stop
# meaning what they say.
#
# `cost_basis_cost:` is for the one case where the transaction cannot state a
# cost at all — every split in one foreign currency, no base-currency figure
# anywhere in it. Where the transaction can, a second copy is refused rather
# than allowed to disagree with it.
#
# What this fixture produces: one error naming the split and both figures.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_update_strategy_respects_cost_basis.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank:USD
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"

2026-01-10 * "Buy 100 USD at 1.35, claiming it cost 9.99"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Bank:USD 100.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.35"
		value: "135.00"
		cost_basis_cost: "9.99 CAD/USD"
	Assets:Bank -135.00 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "1"
		value: "-135.00"
